13 11-04-2025 I.A. No. 1 of 2024 Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.
2. We had issued notice to the informant which has been validly served but no one has appeared on behalf of the informant to oppose the prayer.
3. This interlocutory application has been filed by the appellant seeking suspension of his sentence and release on bail during pendency of the appeal.

He has been convicted vide judgment dated 20.01.2023 and sentenced vide order dated 24.01.2023 by learned Additional Sessions Judge-VI-cum- POCSO Court, Jehanabad in connection with Special POCSO Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.201 of 2023(13) dt.11-04-2025 Case No. 32 of 2020 arising out of Jehanabad Mahila P.S. Case No. 23 of 2020 for the offences punishable under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code (in short 'IPC') and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (in short 'POCSO Act'). He has been ordered to undergo life imprisonment for commission of the offence punishable under Section 376 IPC and Section 4 of the POCSO Act and also to pay a fine of Rs.20,000/- each and in default, he will suffer simple imprisonment for six months more each.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant has taken this Court through the written typed application submitted under the left thumb impression of the wife of the appellant.
At first instance, it is submitted that the wife of the appellant is an illiterate lady who is engaged in selling vegetables.
Her thumb impression has not even been identified by any person on the typed copy of the application.

5. Learned counsel submits that although the allegations in the application giving rise to the present case are serious in nature as according to it, this appellant had sexually exploited one of his own daughters who was aged about 13 years but on perusal of the records/evidences, it would be evident that the appellant has been framed in this case by his wife on account on severe matrimonial discord and differences leading to Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.201 of 2023(13) dt.11-04-2025 separation of the appellant from his wife.
6. Learned counsel submits that according to the informant, she was married with this appellant about 20 years ago and she had six daughters and two sons from the marriage.
She was living in her sasural.
Two of her daughters were already married.

It would also appear that according to the informant, she had come to know from one of her daughters that this appellant was sexually exploiting her for last 3-4 months by taking her to the kitchen room and sometimes, the appellant was tying the victim girl and sometimes, she was being given some money, chocolates and biscuits to allure her.

The informant has herself stated in the written application that she along with her children had left her sasural in the month of February whereafter she had gone to her maiyke at Belaganj in the District of Gaya but she did not disclose this in order to save her reputation in the society.
Thereafter, she started living in a rented house in Jehanabad Town.
She lodged the case after her husband sent her a notice to compel her to live with him.
After receiving notice and getting harassed because of the said notice, she was lodging the case in which she alleged that her husband was sexually exploiting one of her daughters.

7. Learned counsel submits that the written application has been submitted on 02.09.2020 i.e. after seven months of Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.201 of 2023(13) dt.11-04-2025 leaving the sasural and when the informant had received notice from her husband.

8. It is pointed out from the evidence of the informant (PW-5) that she has in her description of the house at sasural clearly stated that there are four rooms and one kitchen in the sasural, there is no latrine or bathroom and there is only one door at the main door of the house, in the rooms there is no door.
It is submitted that according to the informant, the occurrence was taking place inside the house when the daughter was being taken away to the kitchen room and she was being sexually exploited.

It is evident that there is no door in the kitchen and all rooms are open, in these circumstances, it is difficult to believe that when the informant along with her other seven children would be sleeping in the house, the appellant would take one of the children to the kitchen room and shall commit rape on her, that too regularly.
9. Learned counsel submits that PW-6 is the victim girl who has stated that she had never gone to school.

She has stated that the appellant was committing wrong with her prior to seven months from the date of lodging of the case and she has stated in paragraph '11' of her deposition that her mother had seen committing wrong act with her.
This is not, however, the statement of her mother (PW-5).

The victim girl has stated that Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.201 of 2023(13) dt.11-04-2025 there are four rooms and when her father used to commit wrong act with her, she was weeping,
crying and shouting.

It is submitted that the statement of the victim girl in her deposition seems to be not only highly improbable but against the understanding of a normal human brain that in presence of her own mother and other seven siblings, even as she was crying and weeping, her father would be able to commit rape on her.
10. It is pointed out that in paragraph '13', the victim has stated that her father had tied her legs and hands and had committed wrong act with her for ten days.

It is submitted that such statements are only bald allegations and it may be appreciated that in the house where her mother and other brothers and sisters are present, her father would tie her hands and legs and then would commit wrong with her for ten days.

Submission is that the manner in which highly exaggerated and improbable statements have been made by PW-5 and PW-6 would only show that it is a case of false implication with some legal advice and in order to make the allegations serious, the mother of the victim has lodged the case of this nature after seven months of her separately living from her husband.
11.

Learned counsel submits that the medical examination of the victim girl was conducted,
however, the Doctor found that the hymen was old ruptured, there was no Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.201 of 2023(13) dt.11-04-2025 internal injury and there was no recent sign of sexual contact.
12
It is submitted that the appellant is in incarceration for about four and half years.
This appeal is of the year 2023 and is not likely to be heard in near future.
13. Mr. Parmeshwar Mehta, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.

It is submitted that the allegations against the appellant have been proved by PW-5 and PW-6.
14.

Having heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State and upon perusal of the records prima-facie for purpose of the present case, we find at this stage that the wife of the appellant is the informant of this case who has lodged the present case by submitting a written typed application before police under her left thumb impression, after seven months of her separation from the appellant.

The immediate cause for lodging of the FIR is stated in the written application and according to that, her husband had served a notice upon her in the month of July in which he wanted her to come back and live with him.

She has clearly stated that she is not aware of law but because of his threat and notice, she was lodging this case and complaining against her husband of committing sexual exploitation of his daughter.

15. This Court has further noticed that the place of Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.201 of 2023(13) dt.11-04-2025 occurrence is said to be the sasural house of the informant where she was living with her husband and eight children including the victim girl.
Her two daughters were already married.
She has clearly stated that the rooms in the house have no door and there is only door at the main gate.

According to the informant and the victim, the appellant was committing rape on the Ajay Kewat @ Ajay Kebat vs The State Of Bihar on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146880270/
3 victim by taking her to the kitchen room.

sentences.text: The victim claims that she was crying and weeping when she was being subjected to rape but it seems highly improbable that despite her crying in the kitchen room which has no door, neither her mother nor any other brothers or sisters from the family would know it.

The victim claimed that her father had tied her by her hands and legs and had committed wrong with her for ten days, again this story is not inspiring confidence of the Court considering that such occurrence for 10 days would not have been possible in the house where her mother and other members of the family were living.

Prima-facie, this Court finds that the allegations which have been made are though serious in nature, but are not coming from sterling witnesses and the circumstances showing that the FIR has been lodged seven months after separation are such that this Court having further noticed that the appellant has remained in jail for four and half years but the appeal is not likely to be heard in near future is persuaded to grant suspension of sentence Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.201 of 2023(13) dt.11-04-2025 and release of the appellant on bail during pendency of the appeal.

16. Let the sentences be suspended and the appellant above-named be released on bail during pendency of the appeal on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand)
with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-VI-cum- POCSO Court, Jehanabad in connection with Special POCSO Case No. 32 of 2020 arising out of Jehanabad Mahila P.S. Case No. 23 of 2020.

18. It is clarified that the observations made hereinabove are only prima-facie and tentative in nature for purpose of consideration of bail of the appellant and would not cause prejudice to either of the parties.
19. I.A. No. 1 of 2024 stands disposed of accordingly.

20. List this appeal for hearing on its turn.
